column7: Just-in-time defect prediction identifies buggy commits immediately after they are made. This paper presents Commit2Vec, a deep learning approach that learns distributed representations of code changes for defect prediction. We evaluate on the JITGIT dataset and achieve AUC of 0.78, outperforming Random Forest baseline by 0.06. Our method uses neural networks to encode commit messages and code diffs.

Mining software repositories provides insights into software evolution and developer behavior. Code review is a part of the development process that helps identify defects early. Machine learning models can predict which code changes are likely to introduce bugs. This approach has been widely adopted in industry.

Graph neural networks can model code structure for bug detection. CodeGraph-JIT uses heterogeneous graphs to represent commits and achieves state-of-the-art results on benchmark datasets. The approach improves over traditional feature engineering methods by learning representations directly from code. We demonstrate improvements of 7% AUC on JITGIT.

Technical debt is a metaphor for the implied cost of additional rework caused by choosing an easy solution now instead of using a better approach. Code smells are indicators of technical debt and refactoring helps reduce maintenance effort. Our study analyzes 500 open source projects to identify common patterns.

Large language models can assist in code review by suggesting improvements and detecting potential issues. We evaluate GPT-4 and CodeLlama on a dataset of pull requests from GitHub. The models achieve precision of 0.72 for bug detection but struggle with complex architectural issues.

Continuous integration is a software development practice where developers integrate code frequently. Each integration is verified by automated build and test pipelines. CI/CD practices help teams detect defects early and reduce integration problems. Tools like Jenkins and GitHub Actions are widely used.

Clone detection identifies duplicate or similar code fragments across a codebase. Type-3 clones with syntactic modifications are particularly challenging to detect. Our deep learning approach uses AST embeddings to capture semantic similarity. We outperform traditional token-based methods by 15% F1 score.

Software metrics like cyclomatic complexity and lines of code are traditional predictors of defects. However, process metrics capturing developer activity often outperform product metrics. We propose a hybrid approach combining both types of features with graph neural networks.
